This report does not claim every conceivable raw SQL DELETE/REPLACE operation is prevented by that one trigger. Tests must retain the real protections and must not bypass them to manufacture a scenario.
correction.no_bypass_observed: These results expose test assumptions and an overstrong review conclusion; they do not demonstrate that production admitted revoked authority or that a Native/model prompt was sent.

recommended_counterexamples.method: In an isolated fixture transaction, attempt the forbidden UPDATE and assert the specific immutability error. Preserve the trigger. Roll back any newly sealed unused artifact, re-read the original ref/hash/technical/owner tuple and assert it is unchanged. Since authority did not change, a subsequent positive callback is acceptable and must be labeled as unchanged-authority control, not a rejection test.

After BeforeResume, use the established fixture lifecycle from client_workspace_write_authority_windows_test.go: clone the currently bound Artifact, mark validity REVOKED, bump its revision, persist through service.put. Leave runtime_bindings and the Task/dispatch reference untouched. Assert the new Artifact version exists and currentRuntimeBinding now rejects the old frozen reference; then release BeforeModelTurn and require error, zero authorization, no marker and no relaunch.

Keep the foreign Host principal while asserting BeforeModelTurn rejection, no marker and zero authorization. For the later history read, explicitly assert the expected FORBIDDEN, or restore only the test authority after those negative assertions and read history; do not weaken production authentication. Distinguish that restoration from the final-turn authorization phase.

lifecycle_explanation: ensureRuntime creates a runtime binding with INSERT. Existing repository fixtures explicitly document that a replacement profile belongs to a distinct RuntimeRegistration; it is not an UPDATE of an existing binding.

currentRuntimeBinding validates the immutable reference and calls effective. effectiveGraph compares its historical referenced revision with the current Artifact revision and rejects changed revision (STALE_INPUT) before the later validity check. A new revoked Artifact version therefore supplies a meaningful current-admissibility counterexample without replacing the binding.
The production BeforeModelTurn callback reaches currentRuntimeBinding through harnessGate/currentDispatchAdmission/nativeHarnessAdmission, so revocation tests the actual production path.

A failure in the old sealed_binding test triggers its cleanup release of the fixture channel; do not infer zero accepted callback from this failed case. The fixture is in-process and writes no Native/model prompt.
